questions.question: What is HTML?
questions.correct_answer: HyperText Markup Language — the standard language for structuring content on web pages.

questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.correct_answer: HyperText Markup Language.

questions.question: What is the difference between HTML and HTML5?
questions.correct_answer: HTML5 is the latest version with new semantic elements, native media support, canvas, and APIs.

questions.question: What are semantic HTML elements?
questions.correct_answer: Elements that describe their meaning, like <header>, <nav>, <article>, <section>, <footer>.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the DOCTYPE declaration?
questions.correct_answer: Tells the browser which HTML version to use for rendering the page.

questions.question: What is the difference between block and inline elements?
questions.correct_answer: Block elements take full width and start on a new line. Inline elements flow within text without breaking the line.

questions.question: What is the alt attribute used for?
questions.correct_answer: Provides alternative text for images, used by screen readers and displayed when the image fails to load.

questions.question: What is the difference between <div> and <span>?
questions.correct_answer: <div> is a block-level container. <span> is an inline container.

questions.question: What is the <meta> tag used for?
questions.correct_answer: Provides metadata about the HTML document, like character set, viewport settings, and descriptions.

questions.question: What is the difference between <section> and <div>?
questions.correct_answer: <section> represents a thematic group of content with semantic meaning. <div> is a generic container with no inherent meaning.

questions.question: What is web accessibility?
questions.correct_answer: Making websites usable by everyone, including people with disabilities, through proper HTML, ARIA, and design.

questions.question: Why is alt text important?
questions.correct_answer: It helps screen readers describe images to visually impaired users and shows when images fail to load.

questions.question: What is ARIA?
questions.correct_answer: Accessible Rich Internet Applications — attributes that make dynamic content more accessible to assistive technologies.

questions.question: What is the role of tabindex?
questions.correct_answer: Controls whether an element can receive keyboard focus and the order of tab navigation.

questions.question: What is the difference between role and aria-label?
questions.correct_answer: role defines the element's purpose (e.g., role='button'). aria-label provides a text description for screen readers.

questions.question: Why should you use proper heading hierarchy?
questions.correct_answer: Screen readers use headings for navigation. Skipping levels (h1 to h3) confuses the document structure.

questions.question: What is focus visible?
questions.correct_answer: A CSS pseudo-class (:focus-visible) that styles elements only when focused via keyboard, not mouse clicks.

questions.question: What is skip navigation?
questions.correct_answer: A link at the top of a page that lets keyboard users skip past repetitive navigation to the main content.

questions.question: What is the lang attribute?
questions.correct_answer: Set on <html> to declare the page's language, helping screen readers pronounce content correctly.

questions.question: What is WCAG?
questions.correct_answer: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines — a set of standards for making web content accessible to people with disabilities.

questions.question: What is CSS?
questions.correct_answer: Cascading Style Sheets — a language used to style and layout HTML elements.

questions.question: What does CSS control?
questions.correct_answer: Layout, colors, spacing, typography, and visual design of web pages.

questions.question: What is the box model?
questions.correct_answer: Every element is a box with content, padding, border, and margin layers.

questions.question: What is the difference between margin and padding?
questions.correct_answer: Margin is outside the border (space between elements). Padding is inside the border (space between content and border).

questions.question: What is the difference between display: block and display: inline?
questions.correct_answer: Block elements take full width and start on a new line. Inline elements flow within text without breaking the line.

questions.question: What is the difference between position: relative and position: absolute?
questions.correct_answer: Relative positions relative to its normal position. Absolute positions relative to the nearest positioned ancestor.

questions.question: What is CSS specificity?
questions.correct_answer: A set of rules that determines which CSS selector wins when multiple selectors target the same element.

questions.question: What is the !important rule?
questions.correct_answer: A declaration that overrides all other declarations for that property, regardless of specificity.

questions.question: What is Flexbox?
questions.correct_answer: A CSS layout model for arranging items in a single row or column with alignment and distribution controls.

questions.question: What is CSS Grid?
questions.correct_answer: A two-dimensional layout system for creating complex page layouts with rows and columns.

questions.question: What are CSS animations used for?
questions.correct_answer: Creating motion effects on web elements using keyframes and animation properties.

questions.question: What property defines animation duration?
questions.correct_answer: animation-duration — specifies how long one animation cycle takes.

questions.question: What is @keyframes?
questions.correct_answer: A CSS at-rule that defines the stages and properties of an animation sequence.

questions.question: What is the difference between transition and animation?
questions.correct_answer: Transitions animate between two states on trigger. Animations can run automatically, loop, and have multiple keyframes.

questions.question: What does animation-iteration-count do?
questions.correct_answer: Specifies how many times an animation should run. Use 'infinite' for endless looping.

questions.question: What is animation-fill-mode?
questions.correct_answer: Controls how the element applies styles before and after the animation runs.

questions.question: What is animation-timing-function?
questions.correct_answer: Defines the speed curve of the animation, like ease, linear, ease-in, ease-out.

questions.question: Can you animate CSS transforms?
questions.correct_answer: Yes. Transform properties like translate, rotate, and scale are commonly animated for smooth performance.

questions.question: What is will-change?
questions.correct_answer: A CSS property that hints to the browser an element will change, allowing it to optimize rendering performance.

questions.question: What is the performance cost of CSS animations?
questions.correct_answer: Animating transform and opacity is cheap (GPU-accelerated). Animating layout properties like width or top is expensive.

questions.question: What is a CSS selector?
questions.correct_answer: A pattern used to select and target HTML elements for styling.

questions.question: What is the difference between class and id selectors?
questions.correct_answer: Class (.class) is reusable on multiple elements. ID (#id) should be unique per page.

questions.question: What is the universal selector?
questions.correct_answer: The * selector targets all elements on the page.

questions.question: What is the difference between .a.b and .a .b?
questions.correct_answer: .a.b selects an element with both classes. .a .b selects .b elements inside .a elements.

questions.question: What is the > combinator?
questions.correct_answer: The child combinator — selects elements that are direct children of the parent.

questions.question: What is the ~ combinator?
questions.correct_answer: The general sibling combinator — selects all siblings that come after the first element.

questions.question: What is :nth-child()?
questions.correct_answer: A pseudo-class that selects elements based on their position among siblings.

questions.question: What is ::before and ::after?
questions.correct_answer: Pseudo-elements that create virtual elements before or after an element's content for decorative purposes.

questions.question: What is attribute selector?
questions.correct_answer: Selects elements based on their attributes, e.g., [type='text'] or [href^='https'].

questions.question: What is specificity order for selectors?
questions.correct_answer: Inline styles > IDs > Classes > Elements > Universal. Higher specificity wins.
